observation.visible_scene: A white rectangular pillow lies on a patch of charred, ash-covered ground outdoors, surrounded by dry leaves, dirt, and some green moss at the frame edges. The pillow's front face shows a large dark-brown scorch mark with a feathered edge. Orange flames (with a small blue flame near the lower-left corner) burn along the pillow's left side and bottom edge. The camera view is fixed and steady throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The flames flicker and change shape frame to frame: at times they rise higher along the left/top-left edge (e.g. around t=0.15, 0.42, 0.46, 1.23, 1.5), at other times they hug the lower-left and bottom edge more closely, but the overall burning zone (left and bottom of the pillow) persists continuously.
The pillow itself does not move, shift, or collapse; its position and orientation on the ground remain constant across all sampled frames.
The brown scorch mark on the visible face stays roughly the same size and shape from the first to the last frame, with no clearly visible expansion during the excerpt.
The small blue flame at the lower-left corner remains present throughout, varying only slightly in brightness/shape.
Background elements (ash, leaves, moss) show no change, indicating no camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the fire was ignited and what happened before this segment.
Whether the scorch mark later spreads, the pillow collapses, or the fire dies out after this excerpt.
The full duration and outcome of the burning.
The pillow's internal material/filling and the exact fuel sustaining the flame.
uncertain_details: Any very slow growth of the scorch mark or slight settling of the pillow is not reliably distinguishable from frame-to-frame noise at this sampling rate.
The precise cause of the blue flame color (material vs. additive) is not determinable from the images.
Whether the camera is perfectly static or only approximately static cannot be confirmed beyond the visible background, which shows no shift.
